name: Smoked Pork Ribs With Plum Barbecue Sauce

cookwares.name: food mill (strongly recommended) or fine-mesh strainer if using wild plums
chimney starter (if using a charcoal grill)
2- to 3-inch wood chunks (such as oak, pecan, or apple, for smoking)
disposable aluminum drip pan (if using a charcoal grill)

ingredients.name: rice vinegar, divided, plus more as needed
St. Louis–cut pork spareribs, 2 1/2 to 3 1/2 pounds each
mild smoking wood, such as oak, pecan, or apple

instructions.primary_message: For the Sauce: If using wild plums, combine plums and 1/4 cup water in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce heat to low and simmer gently, stirring and mashing plums occasionally with a wooden spoon, until the fruit softens and collapses, 10 to 15 minutes.

Remove saucepan from heat. Immediately pass cooked wild plums through a food mill or press them through a fine-mesh strainer set over a heatproof bowl, separating the pulp and juices from the skins and pits. Discard skins and pits and return plum purée to saucepan.
If using domesticated plums, skip steps 1 and 2. Halve, pit, and finely chop plums, then add them directly to medium saucepan without the water.

To plum purée or chopped domesticated plums in saucepan, add brown sugar, soy sauce, Worcestershire sauce, garlic powder, paprika, cumin, cayenne, celery seed, black pepper, onion powder, allspice, cloves, and 2 tablespoons vinegar and whisk to combine. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce heat to low and simmer, stirring frequently to prevent scorching, until sauce is reduced to about 2 cups and thickened, 20 to 25 minutes.

Using an immersion blender or countertop blender, blend sauce until completely smooth, 1 to 2 minutes. Taste and stir in additional vinegar, 1 teaspoon at a time, until sauce is as tangy as desired. Set aside 1 cup sauce in a small bowl for glazing ribs; reserve remaining sauce separately for serving.

For the Spice Rub: In a small bowl, whisk together brown sugar, kosher salt, paprika, black pepper, and garlic powder until thoroughly combined, breaking up any clumps of brown sugar with your fingers.

For the Ribs: Check the bone side of each rack of ribs for a thin, shiny membrane. If present, slide the tip of a butter knife or the handle of a spoon underneath the membrane to loosen a flap. Using a paper towel for grip, pull off and discard membrane. Pat ribs dry with paper towels, then season evenly on both sides with all of the rub. Let ribs stand at room temperature while you prepare grill or smoker.

If using a charcoal grill, spread a thin, single layer of unlit briquettes over one-third of bottom grill grate. Light one-quarter chimney of briquettes (about 1 1/2 quarts). When briquettes are glowing, pour them over unlit coals to create an indirect heat source. Place a foil drip pan on empty side of grill. Set cooking grate in place, cover, and position top vent over cooler side. Open bottom vent halfway and top vent three-quarters of the way. Let grill preheat to between 225 and 120°C (250°F) (107 and 121°C), about 10 minutes, adjusting vents as needed to maintain temperature. Add 1 wood chunk to hot coals. If using a smoker, preheat it to between 225 and 120°C (250°F) according to manufacturer’s instructions and add smoking wood as directed.

Place ribs, meat side up, on cooler side of grill or on smoker grate. Cook, maintaining a temperature between 225 and 121°C and keeping grill or smoker covered as much as possible, for 3 hours. Add another wood chunk only after the previous one has burned down and smoke has dissipated; do not add wood after the first 3 hours.

After 3 hours, transfer each rack to a double layer of heavy-duty aluminum foil and wrap tightly. Return ribs, meat side up, to cooler side of grill or smoker. Continue cooking, maintaining a temperature between 225 and 121°C and adding unlit coals as needed, until an instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the meat, away from the bones, registers about 91°C, 1 1/2 to 2 hours.

Transfer ribs to a work surface and carefully unwrap; discard foil. Return ribs, meat side up, to cooler side of grill or smoker. Brush each rack with a thin, even layer of reserved plum sauce set aside for glazing. Cover grill and cook for 15 minutes. Brush with a second layer of sauce, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Brush with a final layer of sauce and cook until sauce has reduced to a glossy glaze and a probe inserted between the bones slides into the meat with little to no resistance, about 15 minutes longer. The meat should have receded to expose approximately 0.5 cm of the bone tips.
Transfer ribs to a cutting board and let rest for at least 15 minutes. Slice between bones and serve with reserved barbecue sauce.

description: This Great Plains–inspired take on Kansas City barbecue pairs low-and-slow smoked pork ribs with a sticky, tangy plum barbecue sauce.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 7 hr 15 min to 7 hr 55 min.

Optional or for serving: 1/4 cup water, optional (see note)

Optional substitutions: whole American wild plums → domesticated plums

Notes: Wild plums produce the most distinctive sweet-tart sauce, but domesticated plums will also work. Because domesticated plums are generally juicier and sweeter, the sauce will not require any water but will likely require the full 4 tablespoons of vinegar and may need an additional splash.
If using a pellet smoker, preheat and operate it according to the manufacturer’s instructions, using the manufacturer-recommended pellets; do not use wood chunks.
Cooking times will vary depending on the grill or smoker, weather conditions, and the size and thickness of the ribs. Use the temperature and visual cues in the recipe as guidelines, but rely primarily on texture to determine doneness: A probe inserted between the bones should slide into the meat with little to no resistance.

Make-ahead and storage: The rub can be stored in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 6 months.
The barbecue sauce can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 1 week.
The ribs are best eaten immediately, but leftovers can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 4 days.
author: Jed Portman
